What you're seeing. The road is built from the real left and right edges every 2 m, at the LIDAR height. The car drives the minimum-time line at the simulated speeds. Kerbs mark where that line puts its wheels on the edge, and the line on the road is coloured by speed, from light blue (slow) to dark (fast).

Surroundings. Buildings are OpenStreetMap footprints, with heights from their storey counts where mapped and estimated otherwise. Parkland, the Serpentine and the Long Water come from the LIDAR and the building map. Trees are placed for scenery, not surveyed.

Heights. London is gentle, so Heights can exaggerate the terrain 2× or 4× to make the climbs readable. Building heights stay real.
